system_prompt_style.note: Paper-only; prompt built from intent, messages, history and the optimizer interval. Could arguably be dynamically_composed.

env_context_strategy.evidence_quote: This average iteration count is the KPI passed to the LLM together with the last ten⟨Kp,ι⟩ pairs stored in a small short-term memory.
env_context_strategy.note: Closest value: KPIs and optimizer outputs are injected into the prompt. There is no repository or file context; the domain is network control.

context_compaction.evidence_quote: Keeping the memory to ten entries bounds prompt length
context_compaction.note: Type I memory is a ten-entry window. Type II compaction is not reported.

observation_format.evidence_quote: This average iteration count is the KPI passed to the LLM

tool_call_format.evidence_quote: LLMs produce explicit chain-of-thought and structured artifacts (JSON SLA decisions and rationales)
tool_call_format.note: The actions are structured artifacts (a Kp value or an SLA bid), not tool calls.

tool_count.note: Paper only; no tool registry is available.

edit_primitive.note: Paper only; this is not a file-editing domain.

tool_schema_source.note: Paper only; no tool schema is available.

protocol_standardization.note: Paper only; no source or dependencies are available.

loop_primitives.evidence_quote: The LLM operates as an asynchronous black-box meta-optimizer and is invoked only when P-Control shows signs of sluggishness.
loop_primitives.note: The LLM is triggered by a KPI threshold. Type II is a multi-round negotiation.

multi_agent_topology.evidence_quote: a multi-tenant MAS topology built around a central mediator, typically operated by the MNO, which guides negotiations
multi_agent_topology.note: The Type II mediator plus tenant agents are closest to a mediated peer negotiation; `peer` is also plausible. Type I is a single agent.

human_in_loop.note: Paper only. Humans supply intents but no gating mechanism is described.

short_term_state.evidence_quote: checks past action sets from a short-term memory
short_term_state.note: The short-term memory holds ten ⟨Kp,ι⟩ pairs; structured_task_state is also plausible.

long_term_memory.note: A vector DB is mentioned only as future work.

self_verification.note: The optimizer guard-rail is not a verification check. The LLM judge in the paper is used for evaluation only.

rollback.note: The paper says only that 'observance of deviations could trigger rollback', with no mechanism described.

termination_condition.evidence_quote: If the system satisfies max i|x(k) i − ¯x(k)| < ϵ, we declare consensus convergence
termination_condition.note: Negotiation ends at convergence ('game ends when the spread of the bids shrinks'). No listed value fits; this is the closest.

permission_model.note: Paper only; no configuration surface is available.

tracing.evidence_quote: all traces logged by logs L for audit

guardrails.evidence_quote: Numeric guard-rails and KPI triggers prevent adversarial or hallucinated actions from propagating to the real-time loop.

target_domain.evidence_quote: Implement two concrete agent designs for dynamic RAN control and multi-tenant SLA negotiations.

open_source.evidence_quote: Part of the developed code and results is open-sourced to bolster research efforts of the commu-
open_source.note: The Data availability section promises release upon acceptance; no repository URL is given in the evidence.

model_agnostic.evidence_quote: including the OpenAI gpt-4o API [50] for LLMs, and a plethora of SLMs from different vendor families

primary_artifact.evidence_quote: Upon acceptance, we will share a Python-based RAN simulation framework

first_release_date.note: The evidence shows only v2 dated 3 Sep 2025. The v1 date is not stated, so no fallback date is available.
